- Add an explicit GitOps validation step before any automated promote: run a Helm diff + kubeval on the rendered manifests, then block promotion on diff > threshold.
- In the Ansible playbook section please include idempotency checks (task-level --check) and a dry-run gate. I put a short checklist in the attached "gitops-runbook.pdf".
- We need an infra ticket for the cluster-level RBAC permission that the canary job uses; please open SUP-4321, link the playbook, and assign to Acme ops.

DevOps: if you can confirm what API quotas and ephemeral port ranges look like on your side we can bake that into the preflight. If there are firewall window constraints, call them out now.

Thanks — confirming the maintenance window for Tues 2027-07-06 02:00-04:00 UTC works for staging. A couple of notes from infra: 

1) Ephemeral port range: current nodes use 32768-60999. For the canary burst we recommend extending to 30000-65000 on the NAT gateway; that will require a quick config change but no hardware upgrade.
2) NAT concurrent connections: current soft limit is 12k; if the canary hits >10k concurrent connections we will see 5–7% tail latency increase. We can temporarily raise to 18k for the rehearsal.
3) Firewall: No inbound changes required for rollback, but outbound egress quotas on the per-subnet ACL will be enforced.

Attached is our current quota snapshot and an export of the node network config. Will link SUP-4321 once the ticket is created by Redwood.

Attachments: [Attachment: current-quota-report.csv (text/csv)]

— Acme DevOps

> 1) Ephemeral port range: current nodes use 32768-60999. For the canary burst we recommend extending to 30000-65000 on the NAT gateway; that will require a quick config change but no hardware upgrade.
> 2) NAT concurrent connections: current soft limit is 12k; if the canary hits >10k concurrent connections we will see 5–7% tail latency increase. We can temporarily raise to 18k for the rehearsal.

Thanks — noted. Below is a condensed Terraform/Helm/Ansible checklist I'm proposing to include in the playbook before the rehearsal: 

Terraform (preflight):
- run `terraform validate` and `tfsec` scan on infra modules
- `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` and push plan artifact to CI store
- automated approval gate: compare plan hashes, require 2 approvers for infra change

Helm (preflight + promote):
- render manifests `helm template` and run `helm diff` against live cluster snapshot
- run `kubeval` and a schema check for CRDs used by inference runtime
- signature check: validate chart provenance (artifact signature)

Ansible (idempotency + rollback):
- run playbooks with `--check` and compare changed/failed counts
- include a tagged `rollback` play with explicit state restores (KV cache flush + model symlink revert)
- after promote, run smoke tests (tokenized workload) and capture latency/error metrics to S3 for 30m

Observability:
- CI must capture token-level traces for the canary and store in the play artifacts
- define an automatic abort if 95th latency regresses by >20% or error rate >0.5% for 10m

I'll add these to the gitops-runbook.pdf and create a small Ansible role snippet for the rollback tag. Kim — once SUP-4321 is open, we can add the infra acceptance criteria above.

Irene Choi
